title: LDN 1295: The Giraffe Nebula
explanation:
# The Giraffe Nebula

Deep in the constellation Cassiopeia lurks LDN 1295, a cosmic cloud of dust and gas so thick it swallows the starlight behind it, creating a dark silhouette that stretches across space like a giraffe with its neck craned impossibly high. Our brains naturally see familiar shapes—whether giraffes, squirrels, or faces—in these shadowy interstellar clouds, a quirk called pareidolia that may have once helped our ancestors spot predators in the wilderness.
